newsitem.title: CHINA: China largest antimony oxide producer cuts output.
newsitem.headline: China largest antimony oxide producer cuts output.

text.p: China's Shi Kuang Shan Mining Administration in central Hunan province, the world's largest producer of antimony oxide, has suspended production at five out of seven production lines, an official said on Tuesday.
"We want to limit our production," the official said by telephone from the mine administration in Lengsuijiang city.
The mine suspended production at the five production lines last Wednesday, he said.
International prices of antimony oxide had fallen to about $2,200 per tonne, compared with production costs of $2,800-$3,000 per tonne at Shi Kwang Shan, he said.
"Currently, world prices are not stable. The more product we turn out, the more losses we make," he said. Its mines reported a loss in 1996.
The administration's mines produced an estimated 17,000-18,000 tonnes of antimony oxide in 1996, he said. About 80 percent was exported.
The mining administration was maintaining normal production at the other two production lines to turn out antimony oxide for buyers who already had ordered it for special industrial use.
Antimony oxide is used in products such as construction materials and television tubes.
"Market conditions will decide whether and when to resume our production," the official said. The administration aims to reduce its output by 10 percent in all of 1997 from last year.
"The reduction may be bigger," he said.
It would launch production of zinc and zinc oxide in 1997 to diversify output, he said.
